name: Ramanatheeswarar Temple, Ramanadeecharam
deity: Shiva as Ramanatheswarar (Ramalingeswarar), with the goddess Sarivar Kuzhali
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Ramanadeecharam, a small shrine at Thirukkannapuram near Nannilam, honours Shiva as Ramanatheswarar — the Ramalingeswarar — with the goddess Sarivar Kuzhali. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by Tirugnana Sambandar, it keeps its own quiet place on the Kaveri's southern bank, apart from the great shrines that share its lord's name.

sections.history: Ramanadeecharam, whose historical name is Tiruramanatheechuram, lies at Thirukkannapuram, about 10 km from Nannilam and some 3 km from Thiruchengattangudi, in Tiruvarur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar, counted among the Shiva shrines on the southern bank of the Kaveri. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Ramanatheswarar — also Ramalingeswarar — in the sanctum, with the goddess Sarivar Kuzhali (also Soodikaambal) in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The walled courtyard and modest gopuram keep the form of the Shiva temples of the Nannilam delta.
sections.legends: Shiva is worshipped here as Ramanatheswarar, the Ramalingeswarar, 'the lord of Rama's linga.' The goddess is Sarivar Kuzhali. This is a small, separate shrine, not to be confused with the great jyotirlinga of Ramanathaswamy at Rameswaram, nor with the Vishnu Divya Desam Sowriraja temple that shares the village of Thirukkannapuram; here the Tevaram praise is Sambandar's alone. As with many delta shrines, the fuller sthala purana survives in local tradition and the Tevaram verses.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a village shrine. Pilgrims on the Nannilam stretch of the Paadal Petra temples include Ramanadeecharam among their stops.
sections.experience: At Ramanadeecharam the pilgrim comes to a small shrine of the Ramalingeswarar. Before Ramanatheswarar and Sarivar Kuzhali, in the green Nannilam delta, the visitor finds the unhurried grace of a Tevaram temple, far from the crowds of the great shrines that share its lord's name.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Ramanadeecharam is at Thirukkannapuram, about 10 km from Nannilam and 3 km from Thiruchengattangudi, in Tiruvarur district. Nannilam and Tiruvarur are the nearest towns and rail heads, with buses and taxis to the village.
